note: The shared starting landscape (no boundary chosen).
text: The starting landscape, the same for every boundary: rolling lowland with low ridges and stream valleys running across the boundary. On the front face, flat rock layers over a crust band of even thickness, with the mantle beneath.

note: convergent, stage 0
text: Convergent boundary, early stage. The starting landscape, the same for every boundary: rolling lowland with low ridges and stream valleys running across the boundary. On the front face, flat rock layers over a crust band of even thickness, with the mantle beneath.

note: convergent, stage 0.5
text: Convergent boundary, middle stage. The plates move towards each other. A range is rising along the boundary. On the front face the rock layers bend up with it and the crust thickens into a root beneath it.

note: convergent, stage 1
text: Convergent boundary, late stage. The plates move towards each other. A high range stands along the boundary, with snow on its highest ground. On the front face the rock layers bend up with it and the crust thickens into a root beneath it.

note: divergent, stage 0
text: Divergent boundary, early stage. The starting landscape, the same for every boundary: rolling lowland with low ridges and stream valleys running across the boundary. On the front face, flat rock layers over a crust band of even thickness, with the mantle beneath.

note: divergent, stage 0.5
text: Divergent boundary, middle stage. The plates move apart. The land is sinking into a rift valley between stepped fault scarps, and the shoulders rise slightly. On the front face the layers drop at each fault and the crust thins beneath the rift.

note: divergent, stage 1
text: Divergent boundary, late stage. The plates move apart. The land has sunk into a rift valley between stepped fault scarps, and the shoulders rise slightly. On the front face the layers drop at each fault and the crust thins beneath the rift.

note: transform, stage 0
text: Transform boundary, early stage. The starting landscape, the same for every boundary: rolling lowland with low ridges and stream valleys running across the boundary. On the front face, flat rock layers over a crust band of even thickness, with the mantle beneath.

note: transform, stage 0.5
text: Transform boundary, middle stage. The plates slide past each other. The ridges and stream valleys that cross the boundary are slightly offset sideways: looking across the boundary, the far side has moved to the right. The relief and the crust do not change.

note: transform, stage 1
text: Transform boundary, late stage. The plates slide past each other. The ridges and stream valleys that cross the boundary are clearly offset sideways: looking across the boundary, the far side has moved to the right. The relief and the crust do not change.
